Back: Foundation Models (Gemini, Veo, Nano Banana, Embeddings) -> AI Development (Agent Studio/Garden, Model Garden, Vertex AI / BigQuery ML, notebooks - where ML engineers work) -> AI Applications (Gemini Enterprise App, Notebook - end-user products). Models -> workbench -> shipped product.

Front: Decoding params: temperature, top-k, top-p - and why temp=0 nullifies top-k/top-p?
Back: Temperature reshapes the distribution (low=focused, high=creative). Top-k = sample from the k highest-prob tokens (fixed count). Top-p/nucleus = smallest set whose cumulative prob >= p (dynamic count). Order: temperature reshapes -> top-k/top-p truncate -> sample. temp=0 = deterministic argmax, so there's nothing left for top-k/top-p to prune.

Front: Grounding vs RAG vs tuning - which fixes what?
Back: Grounding = the goal (answers backed by trusted/current sources), implemented via RAG (retrieve -> inject context at inference, no weight change) -> fixes outdated/not-my-data. Tuning = changes the model's weights -> fixes style/format/task performance. Try grounding/RAG first (cheap, updatable); tune only if prompting+grounding aren't enough.

Front: Three tuning approaches by cost, and what each changes?
Back: prompt design (change only the input/examples, no training) < parameter-efficient/adapter tuning e.g. LoRA (FREEZE the base model, train a small set of ADDED adapter weights - not hyperparameters) < full fine-tuning (update ALL model weights; most compute).

Front: GCP model-build spectrum - pick for tabular data in a warehouse + SQL team, no deep ML?
Back: BigQuery ML: train/eval/predict in SQL inside the warehouse, no data movement or separate stack. Spectrum: pretrained APIs (low-code, common tasks) / AutoML (no-code UI) / BigQuery ML (SQL-native) / Vertex custom training (full control).

Front: ML taxonomy: supervised vs unsupervised subtypes + example algorithms?
Back: Supervised (labeled): classification (logistic regression), regression (linear regression). Unsupervised (unlabeled): clustering (k-means), association (association rule learning), dimensionality reduction (PCA). Tell: 'number' -> regression, 'no labels/group' -> clustering, 'A or B' -> classification.

Lets you train, evaluate, and predict ML models in SQL INSIDE the warehouse - no exporting data or standing up a separate ML stack (ML comes to the data). Workflow: CREATE MODEL -> ML.EVALUATE -> ML.PREDICT.

Front: GCP storage + ML hardware quick map?
Back: Unstructured (images/audio/video) -> Cloud Storage (data lake). SQL warehouse/analytics -> BigQuery. Transactional SQL -> Cloud SQL/AlloyDB/Spanner. NoSQL -> Bigtable/Firestore. Hardware: TPUs are matrix-multiply ASICs, far more efficient than CPU/GPU for the dense tensor math in ML.
